observations.why: Imperative directive performing a settled instruction the speaker expects compliance with — not argued for, just issued. Decision-grade by its performed act, but no ratification language or operational rule lifts it higher.

Operational imperative with absolute scope ('all knowledge') — the speaker is instructing a concrete action and expects it carried out. Decision-grade as a performed directive, not yet principle: no identity-level or permanence language.
Flat unhedged assertion presented as fact, but no ratification, no performed act, no operational rule — a confident position still being stated rather than enacted. Claim, not decision.
